title: Common Factors and Multiples in Applications
introduction: Develop secondary mathematical understanding through common factors and multiples in applications.
definition: For the highest common factor, take common prime factors with their smallest powers. For the lowest common multiple, take all prime factors with their largest powers. HCF helps divide quantities into the largest equal groups; LCM helps find when repeating events coincide.

examples.question: Find HCF and LCM of 36 and 48.
Two bells ring every 8 and 12 minutes, starting together.

exercises.question: Two lights flash every 6 and 14 seconds. Next simultaneous flash in seconds?
Cut 36 cm and 60 cm ribbons into longest equal pieces without waste. Piece length?

summary: For the highest common factor, take common prime factors with their smallest powers. For the lowest common multiple, take all prime factors with their largest powers. HCF helps divide quantities into the largest equal groups; LCM helps find when repeating events coincide.
